title: Reactions of Acids with Metals
content:
# Reactions of Acids with Metals

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Write equations for reactions between acids and metals
- Explain why only some metals react with acids
- Test for hydrogen gas
- Describe the observations for these reactions

## Introduction

Many metals react with acids to produce a salt and hydrogen gas. The speed and vigour of this reaction depends on the position of the metal in the reactivity series.

## Key Concepts

### General Equation

$$\text{Metal} + \text{Acid} \rightarrow \text{Salt} + \text{Hydrogen}$$

This is NOT a neutralisation reaction (no water formed).

### Examples

**With hydrochloric acid (→ chloride salts):**
$$\text{Mg} + \text{2HCl} \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2 + \text{H}_2$$
$$\text{Zn} + \text{2HCl} \rightarrow \text{ZnCl}_2 + \text{H}_2$$
$$\text{Fe} + \text{2HCl} \rightarrow \text{FeCl}_2 + \text{H}_2$$

**With sulfuric acid (→ sulfate salts):**
$$\text{Mg} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{MgSO}_4 + \text{H}_2$$
$$\text{Zn} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{ZnSO}_4 + \text{H}_2$$
$$\text{Fe} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{FeSO}_4 + \text{H}_2$$

### Which Metals React?

**Metals ABOVE hydrogen in the reactivity series react with dilute acids.**

| Metal | Reacts with dilute acid? | Vigour |
|-------|--------------------------|--------|
| K, Na, Li, Ca | Yes (DANGEROUS!) | Very violent |
| Mg | Yes | Vigorous |
| Al | Yes (slow start) | Moderate |
| Zn | Yes | Moderate |
| Fe | Yes | Slow |
| Cu, Ag, Au | No | No reaction |

**Metals BELOW hydrogen (Cu, Ag, Au, Pt) do not react with dilute acids.**

### Why Don't Some Metals React?

- Metals below hydrogen cannot displace hydrogen from acids
- They are not reactive enough to give away electrons to H⁺ ions
- The reaction: Metal → Metal ion + electrons doesn't happen

### Observations

| Metal | Observations with dilute HCl |
|-------|------------------------------|
| Mg | Vigorous bubbling, metal disappears quickly, solution warms |
| Zn | Steady bubbling, metal slowly dissolves |
| Fe | Slow bubbling, metal slowly dissolves, solution turns pale green |
| Cu | No reaction, no bubbles |

### Testing for Hydrogen

**Test:** Hold a burning splint at the mouth of the test tube
**Result:** A **squeaky pop** sound

[DIAGRAM: Test tube with metal and acid, delivery tube, burning splint making squeaky pop]

**Why:** Hydrogen is flammable and burns in air:
$$\text{2H}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{2H}_2\text{O}$$

The "pop" is a small explosion.

### Ionic Equation

The ionic equation shows that H⁺ ions are reduced to hydrogen gas:

$$\text{Metal} + \text{2H}^+ \rightarrow \text{Metal}^{2+} + \text{H}_2$$

For example:
$$\text{Zn(s)} + \text{2H}^+\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{(g)}$$

- Metal is oxidised (loses electrons)
- H⁺ ions are reduced (gain electrons)

### Safety Considerations

**DO NOT react Group 1 metals (K, Na, Li) with acids:**
- Reaction is extremely violent
- May cause explosion
- Hydrogen released can ignite
- Very dangerous

**General precautions:**
- Wear safety goggles
- Use dilute acids only
- Keep flames away from hydrogen
- Work in ventilated area

## Worked Examples

**Example 1:** Write the equation for the reaction between magnesium and dilute hydrochloric acid. Include state symbols.

**Solution:**
$$\text{Mg(s)} + \text{2HCl(aq)} \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2\text{(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{(g)}$$

---

**Example 2:** Zinc reacts with dilute sulfuric acid. Describe what you would observe and write the equation.

**Solution:**
**Observations:**
- Bubbles/fizzing/effervescence
- Zinc slowly dissolves/gets smaller
- Solution warms up slightly
- Gas produced gives squeaky pop with burning splint

**Equation:**
$$\text{Zn} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{ZnSO}_4 + \text{H}_2$$

---

**Example 3:** Explain why copper does not react with dilute hydrochloric acid.

**Solution:**
- Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series
- Copper is less reactive than hydrogen
- Copper cannot displace hydrogen from the acid
- Copper cannot give its electrons to H⁺ ions
- Therefore, no reaction occurs

---

**Example 4:** Write the ionic equation for the reaction of iron with dilute acid.

**Solution:**
$$\text{Fe(s)} + \text{2H}^+\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{(g)}$$

Note: Iron forms Fe²⁺ (not Fe³⁺) when reacting with dilute acids.

## Common Mistakes

- **Mistake:** Thinking all metals react with acids
- **Correct:** Only metals ABOVE hydrogen in the reactivity series react

- **Mistake:** Writing Cu + HCl → CuCl₂ + H₂
- **Correct:** Copper does NOT react with dilute HCl - no equation!

- **Mistake:** Forgetting that iron forms Fe²⁺ (not Fe³⁺) with dilute acids
- **Correct:** Fe + 2HCl → FeCl₂ + H₂ (not FeCl₃)

## Practice Questions

1. Write the general word equation for the reaction of a metal with an acid. (1 mark)

2. Write balanced equations for:
   a) Magnesium + hydrochloric acid (2 marks)
   b) Zinc + sulfuric acid (2 marks)
   c) Iron + hydrochloric acid (2 marks)

3. Describe how you would test for hydrogen gas and state the result of a positive test. (2 marks)

4. Explain why silver does not react with dilute hydrochloric acid, but magnesium does. (3 marks)

5. A student adds iron filings to dilute sulfuric acid.
   a) Describe what they would observe. (3 marks)
   b) Write the equation for the reaction. (2 marks)
   c) What colour is the solution formed? (1 mark)

6. Write the ionic equation for the reaction of zinc with dilute acid. Identify what is oxidised and what is reduced. (4 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Effervescence | The production of bubbles of gas |
| Squeaky pop | The sound made when hydrogen burns in air |
| Reactivity series | A list of metals in order of their reactivity |
| Displace | To take the place of another element |

## Summary

- **Metal + Acid → Salt + Hydrogen**
- Only metals **above hydrogen** in the reactivity series react
- Cu, Ag, Au, Pt do **not react** with dilute acids
- **Test for hydrogen:** Squeaky pop with burning splint
- More reactive metals react more vigorously
- **Safety:** Don't use Group 1 metals (K, Na, Li) - too dangerous
- Ionic equation: M + 2H⁺ → M²⁺ + H₂
